text:
lina: Quick brain dump: we keep getting confused by role inheritance for API keys (org-admin -> project-admin -> writer). Thinking about flattening to explicit role bindings only (no implicit inheritance). Pros/cons?

chris: Flattening reduces surprise. Today someone with org-admin accidentally gets writer perms in every project and that bites when rotating keys.

devin: Con: lots of config churn when teams relied on inheritance to bootstrap. We'll need migration shims and tooling to compute effective roles.

lina: Exactly. Proposal: on create_key allow `bindings: [{role: "project:writer", scope: "p-12"}]` only. Deprecate implicit org->project inheritance but provide a transition mode that materializes derived bindings.

tera: How do we show effective permissions in the console? Ops asks for a simple view to avoid mistaken revokes.

chris: Console should show two panels: explicit bindings and derived bindings (during transition). Once migration done, derived collapses. Also add a "why" link that shows the rule chain.

devin: Runtime: policy checks must remain fast. If keys list many explicit bindings, gateway check should still be O(1) for a token. Precompute a bitmap or hash of allowed (resource, action) pairs per key and cache in gateway.

lina: Good point. We'll encode a compact permission vector like `perm_hash` and gateway checks membership. This keeps checks cheap without RPCing policy service.

tera: What about audit logs? We need clear records showing if access was allowed via explicit binding or derived fallback. That helps incident forensics.

chris: Add `authz.allow_reason` field to logs: values {explicit_binding, derived_binding, default_admin, delegation}. That way it's searchable.

devin: Migration plan idea: produce a script that scans orgs for keys with implicit permissions, materializes explicit bindings into a draft metadata field `migrated_bindings:v1`, and notifies owners. Owners can approve or rollback. After N days auto-commit unless there are blockers.

lina: Nice. Need to be careful with service accounts used by infra: auto-commit only allowed for non-critical keys flagged by ops. For flagged keys require manual approval.

tera: For service-to-service auth, we should keep ephemeral tokens (audience-scoped) and avoid giving long-lived keys admin-level scopes. Where long-lived keys exist, add "usage policy" that forbids certain actions (eg. no billing changes).

chris: SDK/API change: `create_key(bindings=[...], usage_policy=["no_billing"] )`. Return a `permissions_preview` on create so caller sees immediate implications.

devin: Tests: unit tests for perm_hash generation, integration test verifying gateway cache TTL and log entry `authz.allow_reason`. Also acceptance tests for migration flow (dry-run -> commit -> revoke).

security-bot: Note: flagging CVE mitigation: keys with org-admin inherited into more than 50 projects will be rate-limited for rotation until owner approval.

lina: Action items: (1) eng-security drafts migration script and acceptance criteria, (2) eng-runtime implements perm_hash and gateway cache semantics, (3) devex/console adds bindings UI + preview, (4) ops defines flagged key list and manual approval workflow. I'll write the short RFC and share a sample `bindings` payload.

chris: Example payload suggestion:

```json
{
  "key_id": "k-zzz111",
  "bindings": [
    {"role": "project:reader", "scope": "p-12"},
    {"role": "dataset:writer", "scope": "d-77"}
  ],
  "usage_policy": ["no_billing"],
  "meta": {"created_by": "lina"}
}
```

lina: Thanks all. I'll include migration dry-run metrics in the RFC and tag teams for review. Ping me for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
